method: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Febrile seizure' (last updated February 2026, PIC endorsed). Every claim is a paraphrase backed by anchors (scripts/anchor.py): verify.py --source re-finds each anchored span in a fresh copy of the source, checks the claim's numbers against it and rejects copying. LICENCE: © The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne; Terms clause 5.2, personal use only; paraphrased and hash-anchored (read at the RCH website Terms and Conditions, clause 5.2). The source's words are NOT reproduced here. Edition 2.0 rebuilds the Wave 1 hand-written page (edition 1.0, 2026-09-22), which quoted RCH verbatim, as a paraphrase of the page re-fetched 2026-09-24. Every Wave 1 claim is carried over except the title of the WA parent resource, which the fresh text no longer shows (see Unresolved). The temperature threshold renders as '380C' on the page; claims give it in words.

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Three headline messages:** the large majority of febrile seizures are benign and need no further work-up · care centres on finding and treating the infection · giving antipyretics will not stop a febrile convulsion happening.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Febrile seizure', last updated February 2026, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Febrile_seizure/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **The seizure does not raise the infection risk:** after a simple febrile seizure, the chance of a serious bacterial infection is the same as with fever alone. Manage the cause of the fever.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Febrile seizure', last updated February 2026, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Febrile_seizure/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Definition:** a young child has a seizure together with fever of at least thirty-eight degrees Celsius (the page renders it '380C'), and has none of: an infection of the central nervous system, an electrolyte disturbance, or previous seizures without fever.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Febrile seizure', last updated February 2026, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Febrile_seizure/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Typical age 6 months to 6 years**; most occur with an uncomplicated viral infection.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Febrile seizure', last updated February 2026, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Febrile_seizure/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Simple** (all four needed): generalised tonic-clonic · lasts under 15 min · fully recovered within 1 hour · no second seizure in the same illness.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Febrile seizure', last updated February 2026, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Febrile_seizure/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Afebrile febrile seizure:** fits the simple pattern but happens during an acute infection with no fever documented.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Febrile seizure', last updated February 2026, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Febrile_seizure/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Complex** (any one is enough): focal features · lasts over 15 min · altered mental state persisting beyond 1 hour · a repeat seizure in the same illness.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Febrile seizure', last updated February 2026, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Febrile_seizure/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Prolonged febrile seizure:** a complex one lasting over 30 minutes; it can be linked to genetic epilepsy syndromes.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Febrile seizure', last updated February 2026, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Febrile_seizure/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Recurrence is likelier the younger the child:** roughly 50% if the first seizure is at 1 year of age, 30% at 2 years.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Febrile seizure', last updated February 2026, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Febrile_seizure/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Family risk:** 1 in 30 in the general population · 1 in 5 with one affected sibling · 1 in 3 when both parents and an earlier child have all had febrile seizures.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Febrile seizure', last updated February 2026, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Febrile_seizure/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **No one gene explains febrile seizures**, although genes have been found in families with the GEFS+ spectrum (genetic epilepsies with febrile seizures plus).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Febrile seizure', last updated February 2026, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Febrile_seizure/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Genetic testing can be advised for certain higher-risk groups**, for example a child under 18 months with a prolonged febrile seizure.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Febrile seizure', last updated February 2026, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Febrile_seizure/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **History:** when the illness began · the likely fever source (viral illness, gastroenteritis, UTI) · the seizure itself: how long, generalised or focal, how long the post-ictal phase, and whether the child is back to neurological baseline.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Febrile seizure', last updated February 2026, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Febrile_seizure/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Also ask about:** other explanations for the event (seizure mimics, cardiac arrhythmia, underlying metabolic disorders) · known neurological conditions · developmental delay or regression · febrile seizures, epilepsy or sudden cardiac death in relatives.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Febrile seizure', last updated February 2026, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Febrile_seizure/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Examination:** look for the infection source, and examine neurologically to confirm the child is back to baseline.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Febrile seizure', last updated February 2026, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Febrile_seizure/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Red flags for CNS infection:** a complex febrile seizure · meningism (bulging fontanelle, stiff neck, photophobia) · reduced consciousness lasting more than 1 hour after the seizure.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Febrile seizure', last updated February 2026, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Febrile_seizure/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Check the skin for neurocutaneous signs:** port-wine stain or angiofibroma on the face, hypopigmented macules, café au lait spots.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Febrile seizure', last updated February 2026, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Febrile_seizure/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Simple febrile seizure: test only what the fever itself needs.** More blood tests and neuroimaging rarely find anything and expose the child to needless painful procedures and/or radiation.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Febrile seizure', last updated February 2026, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Febrile_seizure/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Atypical presentation or complex seizure: targeted tests.** BGL and serum electrolytes to exclude a provoked seizure; ECG to exclude a mimic.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Febrile seizure', last updated February 2026, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Febrile_seizure/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Investigate the child who looks seriously unwell** (as for any febrile child). Red flags for serious infection: complex febrile seizures · altered mental state persisting over 1 hour · features of sepsis, meningitis or encephalitis · not fully immunised against *Streptococcus pneumoniae* or *Haemophilus influenzae* B.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Febrile seizure', last updated February 2026, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Febrile_seizure/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Complex febrile seizure:** CNS imaging is a consideration, but only after discussion with a senior doctor.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Febrile seizure', last updated February 2026, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Febrile_seizure/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Still seizing after 5 minutes? Treat it**, following the acute (afebrile) seizure guideline.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Febrile seizure', last updated February 2026, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Febrile_seizure/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **No routine ongoing antiepileptic medicine.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Febrile seizure', last updated February 2026, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Febrile_seizure/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Talk to the local paediatric team** for a complex febrile seizure, or if a serious bacterial infection may have caused the seizure.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Febrile seizure', last updated February 2026, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Febrile_seizure/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Think about transfer** for respiratory or haemodynamic compromise · a prolonged febrile seizure · altered mental state beyond 1 hour · a child whose needs exceed what the local hospital is comfortable providing.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Febrile seizure', last updated February 2026, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Febrile_seizure/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Discharge is reasonable** once the child is neurologically back to normal after a simple febrile seizure and the underlying illness has been assessed and managed.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Febrile seizure', last updated February 2026, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Febrile_seizure/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Teach every family before they go home:** seizure first aid and a febrile seizure handout; ⚠️ if a seizure lasted over 5 minutes, consider an emergency medication management plan and training parents to give midazolam.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Febrile seizure', last updated February 2026, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Febrile_seizure/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Follow-up:** arrange review for the underlying illness if needed, and consider outpatient paediatric follow-up (below).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Febrile seizure', last updated February 2026, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Febrile_seizure/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Outpatient follow-up for epilepsy risk factors:** a prolonged febrile seizure · epilepsy in the family · neurocutaneous signs on examination · complex febrile seizures that keep recurring · developmental impairment.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Febrile seizure', last updated February 2026, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Febrile_seizure/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Clinic may add EEG, neuroimaging or genetic testing.** The genetic test may suit higher-risk groups: prolonged febrile convulsions under 18 months · febrile seizures after age 6 years · accompanying developmental impairment.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Febrile seizure', last updated February 2026, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Febrile_seizure/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **The page is PIC endorsed and was last updated February 2026.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Febrile seizure', last updated February 2026, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Febrile_seizure/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Parent information is linked from four states:** Victoria, NSW, Queensland and WA febrile seizure sheets.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Febrile seizure', last updated February 2026, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Febrile_seizure/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **The current reference list adds Schonfeld et al. (BMJ 2024; 385:e076814)** on cutting unneeded tests for children with seizures in the ED.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guidelines: Febrile seizure', last updated February 2026, PIC endorsed, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Febrile_seizure/, retrieved 2026-09-24
